title: What the Search Field Returned
description:
Tunde: 'Once inside the dashboard, The Griot tested every input field. The customer search reflects your term straight back into the response — but not where you would hope. It lands inside an HTML attribute, unescaped. A bare <script>alert(1)</script> will NOT fire there: that is not a script context, it is an attribute value. You have to break out of the attribute first, then land an event handler that actually exfiltrates something.'

Amaka: 'This is a simulator — we do not run your JavaScript. We check that your payload has the SHAPE of a working attribute-breakout exfil: it escapes the attribute, fires on an event, and sends data to somewhere an attacker controls. A payload that would not steal a real victim's session does not count. Capture the flag the server emits when your payload is shaped correctly.'

In the pentest finding (task 9) you will name the precise vulnerability class — at least three related classes live in this family; only one matches what you confirm here. In task 5 you meet its stored cousin — do not confuse them. Note the exact payload you send.

Reference: OWASP Top 10 2021 A03 Injection; OWASP XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet (reflected, attribute context); CWE-79 (Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation).

fallback.response: No customers found matching your query. (Note: a bare <script> tag reflects into an attribute here — it will not fire. Look at where your input actually lands, then break out of it.)
